title: From a Ping product to a searchable, alertable log line
lede: Two families of path. The original one (top): PingOne through a webhook forwarder, PingFederate and the gateway tailed from container stdout by a collector that relabels the container name, a Loki store, a viewer and alert rules; that stream is mock here. The paths below it reach Elasticsearch and Kibana: the Privilege SIEM export and logs bridge, a Vector collector on local Docker, and the PingOne webhook subscription. Each new box says whether it was measured.

sub: Reads container logs; tags noise, masks secrets

steps.title: PingOne webhooks take the short path
steps.what: PingOne is SaaS: it has no container to tail. Its events reach the store only because a forwarder receives the webhook and pushes it. This was the ONLY thing in the store until the collector existed.

steps.title: Containers just print
steps.what: PingFederate and the gateway write to stdout. Without a collector nothing ships that anywhere: the lines are visible only to the container runtime.

steps.title: The collector discovers every container
steps.what: It lists containers through the read-only Docker socket and reads their streams, the same permission `docker logs` needs.

steps.title: Relabel turns a container name into a service
steps.what: The container name arrives with a leading slash and a prefix. One relabel rule strips both so every query uses the bare service name. Turn the rule off in the Label lab and every panel goes empty, with no error.

steps.title: The gateway also exposes metrics
steps.what: Metrics are a second feed with a different shape: counters by route and status family. Rules over them use ratios, not counts.

steps.title: The viewer asks the store a question
steps.what: A LogQL query: a label selector, then line filters. The store answers with streams; the viewer shows the lines.

steps.title: Rules watch both feeds
steps.what: A rule fires on a ratio with a traffic floor, so one failed probe on an idle route does not page anyone.

steps.title: Vector reads PingFederate
steps.what: A second collector, Vector on local Docker, reads the PingFederate container log. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Vector reads PingGateway
steps.what: The same collector reads the PingGateway container log. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Vector reads the agent gateway
steps.what: The Privilege agent gateway on local Docker writes a file, not stdout; Vector reads that file too. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Vector writes ping-logs-*
steps.what: Vector tags known-harmless lines as noise and masks secret-looking values before it writes to the ping-logs-* indices in Elasticsearch. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Privilege exports events
steps.what: The hosted gateway and the console send their events to the Privilege SIEM export: console admin changes and runtime events. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Export to ping-siem-events-v2
steps.what: Every exported event lands in the index ping-siem-events-v2, marked console or runtime (privilege_event_kind). Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: The bridge copies the rest
steps.what: Privilege does not export policy decisions, AI Guard verdicts or approvals. The Privilege logs bridge copies them. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Bridge to the same index
steps.what: The bridge writes into the same index, so one Kibana search covers what Privilege exports and what the bridge copied. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Every event type
steps.what: One PingOne webhook subscription for every event type (SSO, MFA, DaVinci, Authorize, Protect, Verify and the rest) posts to pingone-events-LAB. Being switched on now: not measured yet.

steps.title: To ping-logs-pingone
steps.what: pingone-events-LAB writes each event to ping-logs-pingone with a service label taken from the event type (sso, mfa, davinci ...). Being switched on now: not measured yet.

steps.title: Kibana reads it
steps.what: Kibana holds the dashboards, the saved searches and the Security detection rules over these indices. Measured live on 2026-11-08.

steps.title: The loopback forwarder
steps.what: The lab only reads a loopback URL. In Docker the siem profile adds a forwarder on 127.0.0.1:9200 inside the lab that relays to the Elasticsearch port-forward. Measured 2026-11-08: a 30-day read returned events.

steps.title: Real mode read
steps.what: In Real mode {service="privilege-siem"} reads ping-siem-events-v2 through the forwarder, one read-only search. Measured 2026-11-08.

steps.title: Searches tab links into Kibana
steps.what: The Searches tab builds Discover links and KQL for Kibana. The lab never calls Kibana: these are links and text.
